tour.title: Repository Overview
tour.description: Start with the root README to understand this as a personal Arch Linux and Hyprland environment rather than a single application. It introduces the GNU Stow package model, the installation path, and the shared principles of Catppuccin Mocha styling, Vim-style bindings, and composable scripts. The remaining steps show how those principles are implemented across the repository's layers.

tour.title: Bootstrap Flow
tour.description: The installer is the top-level bootstrap workflow: it installs packages, applies Stow packages, provisions the toolchain, and prepares the shell and editor. Read it after the README to see how the quick-start command becomes a complete machine setup. Its orchestration role explains why the supporting scripts are kept small and specialized.

tour.title: Stow Package Engine
tour.description: The shared Stow helpers are the repository's operational core, validating packages before applying or removing their symlinks. The all-packages script builds on these helpers to deploy every recognized package consistently. This separation makes individual package management and full-system bootstrap use the same safety checks.

tour.title: Validation And Repair
tour.description: Once deployment is understood, the doctor script shows how the repository protects its symlinked layout. It validates package markers and ignore files, dry-runs restows, and reports broken links. This is the maintenance counterpart to the installer and a useful first stop when a managed configuration is not behaving as expected.

tour.title: Shell Foundation
tour.description: The desktop layer begins with a deliberately ordered Zsh configuration: core behavior, environment, plugins, completion, aliases, tools, functions, theme, and toolchain initialization. This modular loading order keeps interactive behavior understandable and lets each concern evolve independently. The functions file is broader in scope because it collects reusable development and media workflows.

tour.title: Desktop Configuration
tour.description: Building on the shell, the Omarchy package defines the graphical desktop through focused Hyprland files for startup, bindings, input, monitors, and appearance. This mirrors the repository-wide modular design while keeping compositor changes localized. The package documentation provides the map for extending these settings without confusing them with the surrounding desktop tools.

tour.title: Developer Workspace
tour.description: The developer-tools layer turns the base environment into an editing workflow, with Neovim configured on top of LazyVim and plugins pinned for reproducibility. The initialization and Lazy setup files establish the configuration loading path, while the keybinding guide exposes the user-facing workflow. Yazi follows the same declarative approach for terminal file management, including behavior, plugins, and visual integration.

tour.title: Knowledge Management
tour.description: The Obsidian package is a separate knowledge-management layer that standardizes shared application settings and vault lifecycle workflows. Its README explains vault organization, synchronization, backups, and troubleshooting, while the MCP guide connects notes to coding-agent workflows. The shared plugin configuration makes enabled core capabilities consistent across managed vaults.

tour.title: Agent Automation
tour.description: The agent-automation layer applies the Stow model to AI coding clients: instructions define operating behavior, configuration selects models and MCP servers, and specialist documents establish focused workflows. OpenCode is a representative package because its central configuration combines models, plugins, sharing, and server connections. Gemini policies add explicit safety boundaries for sensitive files and Stow-managed symlinks.

tour.title: Extending The Collection
tour.description: Return to the repository guidance when adding or changing a package: mirror the target directory, document it with PACKAGE.md, and apply it through the same Stow workflow introduced earlier. The toolchain configuration clarifies that language runtimes and developer CLIs are owned by Mise rather than Pacman. Together, these conventions keep the collection composable as it grows across desktop, tools, knowledge, and agent layers.
